title: Southern-style "cornbread" (no corn)
summary: An unsweetened skillet bread with a crisp, buttery crust, in the Southern style — made without any corn.
steps: Put 1 tablespoon of the butter in a 25 cm (10 in) cast-iron skillet and heat it in the oven as it heats to 200 °C (400 °F).
Melt the remaining butter. Stir the lemon juice into the almond milk and leave 5 minutes.
Whisk the almond flour, coconut flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt.
Beat the eggs, soured almond milk and melted butter, then stir into the dry ingredients. Rest 2 minutes so the coconut flour thickens the batter.
Take out the hot skillet, swirl the butter to coat and pour in the batter; it should sizzle.
Bake 20–25 minutes, until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool 10 minutes, then cut into 9 wedges.
dairy_free_notes: With dairy-free butter the crust is crisp but less nutty; a spoonful of bacon fat in the skillet, if you eat it, adds the traditional flavour.
tips: Honestly, it tastes like a savoury muffin rather than corn; serve it where cornbread would go — with chili, greens or soup.

origin.history: Cornbread comes from Native American maize cooking, which European settlers adopted in North America. In the American South it became an everyday bread: usually unsweetened, made with buttermilk and baked in a hot, greased cast-iron skillet for a crisp crust. This version keeps the method but contains no corn.
